definitions.explanation: A type of collar that stands upright and fits close to the neck, or the uniform featuring such a collar. In Japan, typically refers to the traditional boys' school uniform (gakuran) with its stiff, buttoned-up standing collar.

examples.japanese: {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{学生服|がくせいふく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: To wear a stand-up collar school uniform.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The {詰|つ}め{襟|えり} is iconic of Japanese boys' school uniforms, known as ⟦{学|がく}ラン→学ラン：18414_gakuran⟧. The design was originally inspired by European military uniforms and became standard in Japanese schools during the Meiji era. While many schools have switched to blazers, the {詰|つ}め{襟|えり} remains a recognized symbol of male student life in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{制服|せいふく}→制服：03086_seifuku⟧ (stand-up collar uniform)
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{学生服|がくせいふく} (stand-up collar school uniform)
- {詰|つ}め{襟|えり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧ (to wear a stand-up collar uniform)

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{詰|つ}める→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧ (to pack tightly, to close up) + ⟦{襟|えり}→襟：06487_eri⟧ (collar) — a collar that is closed up tightly around the neck.
